newsitem.title: UK: UK's CrestCo considers raising extra cash - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK's CrestCo considers raising extra cash - paper.

text.p: The board of CrestCo, the Bank of England-led group developing a computerised share registration system, is considering asking for more money from its 60 backers in order to extend the system's transition period beyond the April deadline, the Times said.
The CrestCo board meets on Monday to consider postponing the deadline to complete the transition to electronic settlements following software problems and complaints from users.

The company is believed to have already used most of a 35 million sterling ($58.8 million) loan facility and has to decide if it can reschedule the transfer of 17 blue chip shares within its present timetable and budget, the newspaper said.
Many in London's financial district say this is impossible and that the transition period should be extended until September, the paper reported.
A five-month extension would cost the London Stock Exchange much more than the 18 million sterling ($30.2 million) it has set aside for transfering shares from Talisman, the current system.
